transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-11-14
Start time: 15:00 PT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Miles (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Alex Carter (Holloway CTO), Maya Reynolds (Holloway CISO), Dr. Isaac Lee (Head of AI Ops), Sara Kim (Security Architect)

Summary (auto): Quick scoping call to align on security/compliance for a small pilot. Primary asks: SOC2 artifacts, SAML test, RBAC mapping, audit log retention and export, KMS integration options, and a benchmark plan to validate latency/cost.

[00:00] Jordan (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros? we got about 50 minutes.
[00:12] Alex (Holloway): Alex here, CTO. we'll be running a pilot across our clinical search and triage workflows.
[00:18] Maya (Holloway): Maya, CISO. i'm mostly here to understand the compliance posture and what level of evidence we need for SOC two, iso, and logging.
[00:27] Priya (Redwood SE): Priya, solutions engineer on the inference side. i'll own the benchmarks and network setup.
[00:34] Sara (Holloway): Sara, security architect. i'll coordinate SSO and the network folks.
[00:40] Isaac (Holloway): Isaac, head of AI ops, will be involved in data prep and runbooks.

[01:05] Jordan: Cool. high level: we propose a 4-week pilot to validate quality and performance, and a short benchmark ahead of kickoff to size the Dedicated capacity or confirm hosted is fine. main security asks i think are SOC two artifacts, sso integration for SAML, RBAC mapping and audit logs - is that right maya?
[01:20] Maya: Yeah, that covers it. we need to see SOC & ISO attestation, access controls - role separation, and audit logs with retention for 1 year for the pilot. also K-M-S integration or key management options because patient data is sensitive.

[02:10] Priya: quick note on KMS: Redwood supports both customer-managed KMS via our Private deployment and integration for hosted customers with customer KMS in some cloud regions. there's also envelope encryption options. i'll share our security doc links after the call.
[02:35] Sara: when you say private deployment, do you mean on-prem or VPC? we have strict egress rules so on-prem might be tricky.
[02:44] Priya: both. Private can be customer-managed VPC where control plane is isolated and data plane stays in your VPC, or fully on-prem in air-gapped setups. for most pilots we do a VPC peering or AWS PrivateLink approach.

[03:10] Alex: timeline wise we want the bench results before our quarterly security review on Dec 5, so ideally benchmarks this week or next.
[03:18] Jordan: ok, target bench run by 2028-11-20; then we can do pilot kickoff week of 11/27 if approvals come through.

[04:00] Priya: on benchmarks, we recommend a synthetic workload of ~50k tokens/day for 3 days to get a stable latency/cost estimate and a second stress test to validate throughput for peak windows. we'll post a template.
[04:25] Isaac: can you detail what the sample payload looks like? our triage uses short prompts plus long context (patient notes). sequence lengths vary — sometimes 1k-2k tokens.
[04:40] Priya: yep, we need a mix: short prompts (50-200 tokens) and long context runs (1k-2k). we'll test with quantized model variants and measure 95th pct latency, cost per 1k tokens, and token throughput.

[05:30] Maya: audit logs — we need immutable logs of who called the model, request/response metadata (not full PII), and export capability to our SIEM. retention for pilot: 12 months. is that doable?
[05:45] Priya: Redwood stores admin and request-level logs. for hosted we have configurable retention and log export to S3 or push to Splunk/Datadog via forwarder. for Private, logs reside in your account and you fully control retention.
[06:05] Sara: format detail — do logs include prompt text by default? we need the option to redact or avoid storing full prompt body for PHI.
[06:15] Priya: by default we capture request metadata and can redact prompt bodies. we also support token-level scrubbing and custom redaction rules. we'll include the doc that explains fields and redaction controls.

[07:00] Jordan: on RBAC, can you outline typical role mapping for enterprise? what roles do you expose?
[07:12] Priya: typical roles: admin, devops/infra, app-admin, reader/audit. we support SSO via SAML and SCIM for provisioning. RBAC policies can be mapped to groups from your IdP. for Private deployments you can also enforce subnet-level restrictions.
[07:35] Maya: SCIM provisioning is key for us. we need automated deprovisioning when folks leave. also MFA enforcement from our side.
[07:45] Priya: SCIM + SAML works fine; MFA is enforced via the IdP. we'll need a test IdP account to run SAML assertions.

[08:30] Alex: what about SOC two docs — do you have a public SOC 2 report or an attestation letter?
[08:38] Jordan: we can share our SOC 2 Type II report under NDA and ISO 27001 certificate summary. i'll attach links to the compliance pack and the contact at our security team.

[09:05] Isaac: curious about model behavior logging — we want to capture model version, quantization state, and selection used per request to correlate regressions. is that available?
[09:15] Priya: yes, request metadata includes model id/version, quantization profile, hardware type. for Hosted we surface these in the request logs and console; for Private you have full control and those fields are exported to your SIEM.

[10:00] Sara: for data privacy: can you confirm data at rest encryption and key separation?
[10:08] Priya: data at rest is encrypted in our storage. for hosted, disk encryption uses provider-managed keys by default, or you can bring-your-own keys (BYOK) in supported regions; Private gives you full control with KMS/HSM.

[10:30] Jordan: shifting to success criteria — what would make this pilot successful from Holloway perspective?
[10:38] Alex: for us success is 1) latency under 300ms p95 for short prompts and under 1s p95 for long context inference in the majority of runs, 2) integration with SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning, 3) audit logs exported to our SIEM with 12-month retention, and 4) no compliance gaps in SOC2 artifact review.
[11:00] Maya: and security acceptance: documented KMS approach, redaction strategy for PHI, and proof of log immutability for audit.

[11:40] Priya: we'll propose acceptance tests: automated latency tests (short/long), SAML test with success/failure cases, RBAC validation matrix, and log export verification to your SIEM.

[12:20] Jordan: on sizing: based on initial numbers you shared — triage throughput at peak ~20 reqs/min with avg 800 tokens each — that equates to roughly 960k tokens per hour? maybe we should double check math.
[12:35] Isaac: sorry, maybe i wasn't clear. peak is 20 concurrent users, typical batch size is 2-3 calls per minute each. so peak token/sec is lower. i'll send a spreadsheet with real numbers.
[12:48] Priya: perfect. we'll use that spreadsheet to model cost and recommended instance types. rough rule: if you have many long-context requests we lean to higher-memory GPUs and enable KV caching where applicable.

[13:30] Alex: for benchmarks, can you run both hosted and a dedicated config so we can compare cost/latency?
[13:38] Priya: yes, we can run a hosted baseline and a dedicated config with identical model and quantization settings. we'll include cost-per-1k-token estimates.

[14:05] Maya: what about data residency — some patients are in CA and EU — are there region guarantees?
[14:13] Jordan: we support region pinning on Dedicated and Private. Hosted can be provisioned in specific cloud regions; we'll flag any region limitations in the compliance pack.

[14:40] Sara: about network: do you require open egress? we often restrict egress to approved endpoints.
[14:50] Priya: for Hosted we require outbound to Redwood endpoints; we provide an allowlist of IPs and domains. For Private, data plane stays inside your VPC and there is no external egress unless configured.

[15:20] Alex: are there any legal/contractual clauses around data usage? we need assurances that data won't be used to train models.
[15:29] Jordan: Redwood has a clear data non-training clause for enterprise customers; pilot contract will state that data is not used for model training and we'll include that language in SOW.

[16:00] Isaac: benchmarking detail: do you capture end-to-end latency including network and client SDK overhead?
[16:07] Priya: yes, we do end-to-end measurements and also server-side tokenization and generation time. we'll provide both to help you isolate network noise.

[17:00] Maya: regarding SOC 2, would you be able to provide the report with a bridge letter if dates are off?
[17:08] Jordan: yes, we'll provide the latest SOC2 Type II and can discuss a bridge letter if required.

[17:45] Sara: auditability — do you support immutable log storage or append-only audit streams?
[17:53] Priya: we support append-only log streams and can offer write-once object storage for audit trails in Private deployments; hosted can export to your write-once store as well.

[18:25] Alex: what's the expected turnaround time to set up SAML test accounts?
[18:32] Priya: once we get SAML metadata and a test IdP entry, we can set up a test connection in ~48 hours. SCIM provisioning test typically takes a bit longer, around 3-5 business days to validate group-sync mapping.

[19:10] Maya: do you have automated evidence for controls or is it all manual?
[19:16] Jordan: some evidence is automated (log exports, config snapshots) and some is artifact/manual (policies, process docs). our compliance pack lists what's automated vs manual.

[20:00] Isaac: about redaction, can we do inline redaction rules that run before logs are persisted? we need PII to never land in long-term logs.
[20:10] Priya: yes, we have pre-ingest redaction hooks. you can provide regex or named entity rules and we can validate on the benchmark data.

[21:00] Alex: on the pilot length — 4 weeks enough to validate? we want to ensure ops runbooks and rollback plans are exercised.
[21:08] Jordan: 4 weeks is typical; first week is integration and SAML, week two benchmark runs, week three pilot traffic, week four wrap-up and final acceptance tests. we can extend if needed.

[22:00] Maya: will there be an SLA during pilot? we need at least 99.5% availability for critical endpoints.
[22:07] Jordan: pilots run under a best-effort posture, but for Dedicated we can contract an SLA. we can provide target latency and availability numbers in the SOW; for pilot we'll commit to support response times.

[23:00] Priya: technical detail — for long-context inference we recommend enabling KV cache and using the large-memory instance class. we'll show cost delta in the benchmark report.

[24:00] Isaac: how do you handle model rollouts & version pinning? we need stable versions for audit reproducibility.
[24:08] Priya: you can pin model versions on a per-route basis; rollouts are via canary with traffic split. all rollout events are logged.

[25:00] Sara: in terms of audit logging fields, can you export enriched logs that include model version, request ID, user ID (mapped to SCIM), and redaction marker?
[25:10] Priya: yes — we'll include a log schema example and map fields to your SIEM.

[26:00] Jordan: ok let's recap next steps (quick).
[26:05] Jordan: 1) Jordan will send SOW + compliance pack + SOC2 links (due 11/17). 2) Holloway to share spreadsheet with real workload numbers and network diagram (due 11/18). 3) Priya will run benchmark template hosted + dedicated and share results (due 11/20). 4) Coordinate SAML test window (target 11/22). 5) Confirm pilot kickoff week of 11/27.

[26:50] Alex: sounds good. minor question on pricing — will you provide both pilot pricing and estimated committed pricing?
[26:58] Jordan: yes, pilot pricing is a short-term rate and we'll include committed capacity options with reserved pricing in parallel.

[28:00] Maya: any known blockers from your side for the pilot?
[28:05] Priya: only blocker is we need the SAML metadata and network contacts for allowlist, and sample anonymized data for redaction tests. otherwise we're clear.

[29:00] Sara: ok we'll get the test IdP metadata and a staging dataset by friday (11/18).

[30:00] Alex: one more ask — can you run a quick privacy impact assessment doc for the pilot? helps the privacy office.
[30:10] Jordan: yes we have a short PIA template we can fill and share.

[31:00] Priya: quick technical caveat: if you want absolute p95 latency under 300ms for long context that's tough; short prompts are achievable, long context depends on model and hardware. we'll show realistic numbers in the benchmark.

[32:00] Isaac: understood. also want to capture model hallucination baseline — we'll include a small eval set for quality checks.

[33:00] Priya: please share the eval set with examples and acceptance thresholds (e.g., F1 or manual review pass rate).

[34:00] Maya: are backups or snapshots of logs available for forensic needs?
[34:07] Priya: yes, we can configure periodic snapshots and store them in your S3 bucket for forensic retention.

[35:00] Alex: any encryption-at-rest caveats in some regions?
[35:06] Jordan: occasionally some cloud regions limit BYOK; we'll flag any region-specific constraints in the compliance pack.

[36:00] Sara: legal side: we'll want the data non-training clause explicitly in the pilot agreement and a mutual NDA.
[36:08] Jordan: yes, we'll include that in the draft SOW and NDA.

[37:00] Priya: i'll follow up with the benchmark plan doc now and set up a repo with results.

[38:00] Isaac: curious about telemetry — do we get per-route dashboards and token-level cost breakdown?
[38:09] Priya: yes, Redwood Console provides per-route model usage, token breakdown, p95 latency and cost attribution. we can share a demo screenshot.

[39:00] Alex: any automation for failover between dedicated and hosted? we want graceful degradation if dedicated capacity is saturated.

[39:10] Priya: yes, smart routing allows fallbacks to compatible hosted models; policy controls let you prefer Dedicated and fallback to Hosted with limits. we'll demo the rollout.

[40:00] Maya: would you support an external auditor review during pilot?
[40:08] Jordan: we support auditor access under NDA for review of relevant artifacts and can coordinate a read-only view for auditors.

[41:00] Sara: are there costs for log exports or SIEM integrations?
[41:06] Priya: small egress/storage charges may apply depending on volume; we'll include estimates in the benchmark cost sheet.

[42:00] Alex: ok final checks — any missing items?
[42:05] Maya: just to reiterate retention one year for logs and the need for redaction pre-ingest.
[42:12] Jordan: noted.

[43:00] Jordan: thanks everyone. we'll action the items and reconvene after benchmark results.
[43:10] Alex: thanks, talk soon.

[44:00] (meeting wrap, informal chat)
[51:45] End of recording.

Notes on transcript quality: automatic transcription had minor mislabels (SOC two -> SOC2, K-M-S spelled out in places), some speaker overlap at 38:00-39:30 where Alex and Priya talk over each other.

References and shared artifacts mentioned:
- Redwood compliance pack link (to be sent under NDA)
- Benchmark template (Redwood/benchmarks/triage-template.csv)
- Sample SOW (draft)
- PIA template

Acceptance criteria (as captured):
- p95 latency targets: short prompts < 300ms, long-context < 1s (goal, to be validated in benchmark)
- SAML SSO + SCIM provisioning successful in test IdP
- Audit logs exported and ingested to Holloway SIEM with 12-month retention
- SOC2/ISO artifacts reviewed and no critical gaps identified
- KMS approach agreed and redaction rules validated

End transcript.
